page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft custom ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a 3.4 GHz clock speed without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 128.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. An integrated 1,890 GB local NVMe SSD delivers fast temporary block storage directly to the host without attaching external disk resources.

Performance benchmarks show pronounced multi-threaded execution and data streaming capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, the server scores within the top 25% of tested systems, corroborated by strong results in Clang software compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem shows top-tier throughput, sustaining uncached read speeds of 448.6 GB/sec and write speeds of 188.32 GB/sec, which supports top-tier PassMark database operations benchmark results. Static web serving throughput reaches 52.38 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the average tier.

Resource efficiency is anchored by dedicated ARM core distribution, avoiding hyperthread contention and lowering thermal overhead relative to x86 alternatives. A primary hardware tradeoff is the total absence of discrete GPU acceleration and x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, making the instance ill-suited for large AI model inference, where 70B parameter prompt processing falls into the lowest percentile. With its combination of sustained multi-core compute, high memory bandwidth, and substantial local NVMe storage, the D32pds_v6 is suitable for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving clusters, CI/CD build runners, and ETL processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by 32 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz with no simultaneous multithreading. It features 128 GB of RAM maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside 1,890 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage and 128 MB of L3 cache. Benchmark testing indicates top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec for uncached reads and 188.32 GB/sec for writes, coupled with top-tier database operation performance. Multi-threaded processing shows strong results across stress-ng, Clang compilation, and decompression suites, whereas single-core performance remains average. Without hardware GPU acceleration, large language model prompt evaluation is restricted. The combination of dedicated physical cores, abundant memory throughput, and high-speed local disk renders this instance an efficient solution for databases, continuous integration, static web hosting, and containerized microservices.
